subject: How to run contrasts tests in R Lavaan?

messages.author: bec3b6c763e426c0
messages.subject: How to run contrasts tests in R Lavaan?
parts:
Context:

I have a model that looks like this (see image).


Treatment A has three levels and Treatment B has two levels. I am using a between-subject design. I used dummy variables to model Treatment A (D_A1, D_A2, D_A3,) and Treatment B (D_B1, D_B2), dropping one level from each from the SEM model.

DV1 and DV2 are latent variables, each measured with several items and treated as continuous.

Fit between A and B is calculated as follows:

 

I modeled Fit with two dummy variables using the staircase coding approach:


Using R lavaan, I ran the following SEM model and obtained the results:

model <- '

          ### Measurement Model

          DV1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3

          DV2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6     

      ## Structural Model

      DV1 ~ D_A2 + D_A3 + Fit_D1 Fit_D2

      DV2 ~ D_A2 + D_A3 + D_B2 + DV1    

      '

## Fit model to data

fit <- sem(model, data=mydata,

                  estimator="MLR", #MLR adjusts chi-square and SE for non-normality

                  missing = 'fiml', # FIML handles missing data

                  fixed.x=T, #cov of exogenous manifest vars taken from sample cov matrix

                  meanstructure=TRUE) #To see results of treatment contrasts

 

Questions:

I would like to now conduct post hoc analyses to examine the contrasts between the levels of the treatments (as well as the fit variable).

1.       What are the meaningful contrasts that can be examined in my model?

2.       How can I set up these contrast tests in R?

 For example, in the SEM function, I set the option meanstructure=TRUE, but I am not sure how this will provide the contrasts.

Another option is to use emmeans, but I am not sure how to use it. For example, when I try the following function, I get a warning message about a perfect fit (see below).

 emmeans(fit, pairwise ~ D_A3 + D_B2, lavaan.DV = c("DV1","DV2"), at = list(D_B2= c(0,1)))

 

Warning messages:

1: In summary.lm(object, ...) :

  essentially perfect fit: summary may be unreliable

2: Not all parameters have been estimated.

This is usually caused by a missing mean structure.

Fixing estimates for these parameters at 0.

3: Not all parameters are included in the VCOV matrix.

Perhaps some are fixed with a modifier, or the mean structure is missing.

Fixing SEs for these parameters at 0.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: How to run contrasts tests in R Lavaan?
parts:
On 11/16/22 20:41, shamel...@queensu.ca wrote:
> I would like to now conduct post hoc analyses to examine the contrasts
> between the levels of the treatments (as well as the fit variable).
>
> 1. What are the meaningful contrasts that can be examined in my model?
> 2. How can I set up these contrast tests in R?

Not sure about 1., but for 2., you need to add labels to all parameters
that are involved in your contrast. For example:

DV1 ~ a*D_A2 + b*D_A3 + c*Fit_D1 + d*Fit_D2

Then, you can use lavTestWald() to test the hypothesis that any
(typically linear) combination of these (labelled) parameters equals
zero. See the man page of lavTestWald() for examples.

Yves.
